key_concepts: Plants have roots, stems, and leaves with distinct functions
Roots absorb water and minerals from soil through root hairs
Xylem tissue transports water and minerals upward from roots to leaves
Phloem tissue transports sugars and organic molecules from leaves to other plant parts
Photosynthesis in leaves produces sugars and organic molecules
Transpiration from leaves creates a suction force that pulls water upward
The human digestive system breaks down food into absorbable nutrients
Humans and plants are interconnected through nutrient exchange in ecosystems
Plant vascular structures can be observed in stem cross-sections under a microscope
Colored water moving through celery demonstrates water transport in plant vascular tissue
